hero.headline: FBI fires analysts who worked on memo linking Catholics to extremism
hero.body:
The FBI has informed multiple intelligence analysts they are being fired for their work on a memo that linked Catholic ideology to potential domestic extremism. The terminations mark the latest fallout from a document that drew widespread criticism from religious groups and lawmakers when it surfaced.

The memo, which originated from the FBI's Richmond field office, suggested that some Catholics who prefer traditional Latin Mass might be susceptible to radicalization. The document proposed developing sources within Catholic parishes and using church events for investigative purposes. After the memo became public, FBI Director Christopher Wray ordered it withdrawn and apologized, calling it a product that did not meet bureau standards.

The analysts being terminated had worked on the memo's creation and distribution. FBI officials have characterized the document as poorly researched and lacking proper oversight before it was circulated internally. The memo drew sharp rebukes from Catholic organizations and members of Congress, who argued it improperly targeted religious Americans based on their faith practices.

The firings represent a significant personnel action in response to the controversy. Federal employee terminations typically follow internal review processes, and the analysts involved may have appeal rights under civil service protections. The FBI has not publicly disclosed how many analysts are being let go or provided details about the internal investigation that preceded the terminations.

The episode has raised broader questions about FBI training and oversight of intelligence products, particularly those touching on constitutionally protected activities like religious worship. Some lawmakers have called for additional reforms to prevent similar incidents. The bureau has said it is reviewing its processes for vetting intelligence assessments before they are shared internally or with law enforcement partners.

cards.headline: US strikes Iranian radar sites after Tehran launches drones toward Strait of Hormuz
cards.body:
The United States struck radar installations on Iran's Qeshm Island, with US Central Command describing the action as a defensive response to Iranian drone launches directed toward the Strait of Hormuz. The military exchange marks a significant escalation in tensions between Washington and Tehran at one of the world's most strategically important shipping routes.

According to US officials, Iran launched attack drones toward the Strait of Hormuz, prompting the American strikes on radar sites. The narrow waterway between Iran and the Arabian Peninsula handles approximately one-fifth of global oil supplies, making any military activity in the region a matter of international concern.

The confrontation occurred amid broader regional instability. Israel and Lebanon agreed to renew their ceasefire arrangement even as the US-Iran military clash unfolded. The military activity also preceded a deadly drone attack on Kuwait's airport, which occurred as a result of the escalating US-Iran skirmish, according to reporting from the Wall Street Journal.

The Strait of Hormuz has long represented a critical flashpoint in US-Iran relations. Iran has previously threatened to close the waterway during periods of heightened tension with Washington. The strait measures only 21 miles wide at its narrowest point, making it vulnerable to disruption. However, Iran's foreign minister Abbas Araghchi stated that the country had not closed the strait. He said Iran imposed restrictions on vessels belonging to countries involved in attacks against Iran while offering assistance to other nations navigating the vital waterway. Araghchi indicated Iran was prepared to ensure safe passage for countries such as Japan if they coordinated with Tehran.

Several NATO members and other US-allied nations have pledged to join efforts ensuring safe passage through the strait of Hormuz. The joint statement from leaders of more than a dozen nations, including the UK, France, Germany, Japan, Canada, South Korea, Sweden and Bahrain, did not provide specific details on how they would accomplish this goal.

The US is reportedly preparing to send three additional warships and thousands more troops to the Middle East. However, President Trump said he was considering winding down the US war on Iran, though he rejected ceasefire discussions, saying "we can have dialogue but I don't want to do a ceasefire. You don't do a ceasefire when you're literally obliterating the other side."

US Central Command's characterization of the action as self-defense indicates Washington is framing the operation as a response to an immediate threat rather than a preemptive strike. Iran has not yet publicly confirmed damage to its radar installations or responded directly to the US account of the incident. The military exchange demonstrates how quickly tensions can escalate in a region already experiencing multiple concurrent conflicts.

cards.headline: Stock Market Suffers Worst Day of Year on Strong Jobs Data
cards.body:
The S&P 500 declined 2.6 percent on Friday, marking its worst single-day performance of 2026 and ending nine consecutive weeks of gains. The Dow Jones Industrial Average fell 695 points, while the Nasdaq experienced steeper declines, dropping 4 percent in its largest one-day loss since April 2025. The broad-based selloff reflected a sharp reversal in market sentiment after weeks of sustained gains.

The market downturn followed a stronger-than-expected employment report showing U.S. employers added 172,000 jobs in May, with the unemployment rate holding steady at 4.3 percent. This resilient labor market data prompted investors to reassess expectations for Federal Reserve interest rate cuts. A robust jobs market typically signals that the central bank will maintain elevated interest rates to address inflation concerns, reducing the likelihood of near-term policy easing. Treasury yields jumped in response to the employment figures as traders adjusted their outlook for prolonged higher rates.

Technology stocks bore the brunt of Friday's decline, with semiconductor companies experiencing particularly sharp losses. The tech-heavy Nasdaq index closed significantly lower as investors retreated from momentum stocks that had driven recent market strength. Chip stocks, including companies like Broadcom and Intel, suffered substantial declines as the semiconductor sector weakness extended across the industry.

The May jobs report demonstrated underlying labor market resilience despite rising inflation and economic uncertainty stemming from ongoing conflict in the Middle East. The unexpectedly strong employment numbers contrasted with earlier concerns about economic softening and forced market participants to recalibrate their positions on potential Federal Reserve policy changes.

The sharp market reversal represents a significant shift after sustained period of gains. Investors now must contend with the prospect of interest rates remaining elevated for an extended period, which typically exerts downward pressure on stock valuations, particularly in growth-oriented sectors like technology. Market participants are repositioning their portfolios based on the likelihood that the Federal Reserve will delay rate cuts given the strength of the labor market.

The selloff underscores the complex relationship between economic strength and market performance. While strong employment data typically signals economic health, it simultaneously indicates that the central bank may maintain restrictive monetary policy longer than investors had anticipated. This dynamic created a challenging environment for growth stocks that benefit from lower interest rates.

Friday's decline marked the market's worst performance in several months, demonstrating how quickly sentiment can shift in response to economic data and changing expectations about Fed policy. The tech sector's particular vulnerability reflected investors' reassessment of valuations for companies with high growth expectations that depend on favorable interest rate environments.

cards.headline: U.S. Job Market Adds 172,000 Positions in May
cards.teaser: Employers added more jobs than expected last month despite ongoing inflation pressures on consumers.
cards.body:
U.S. employers added 172,000 jobs in May, marking the third consecutive month of job growth. The unemployment rate remained steady at 4.3%. However, wage gains slowed and likely failed to keep pace with inflation.

Many of the new positions were concentrated in restaurants, bars, and hotels. Despite the resilient labor market, rising inflation and economic uncertainty continued to weigh on consumer finances and broader market sentiment.

cards.headline: EU moves toward partial membership plan for candidate countries
cards.teaser: European leaders discussed a phased integration approach for nations seeking to join the bloc.
cards.body:
The European Union edged closer to adopting a partial membership framework for countries waiting to join the bloc, with leaders discussing ways to speed integration for Western Balkan nations. The proposal would allow candidate countries to access some EU benefits before completing the full accession process, which can take years or even decades.

German Chancellor Friedrich Merz said the EU would begin integrating Western Balkan countries under the new approach. European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen expressed optimism that Montenegro could join the bloc by 2028 following a Balkans summit. The push comes as the EU seeks to counter Russian and Chinese influence in countries on its periphery and address a longstanding expansion deadlock.

cards.headline: FDA investigating baby botulism outbreak with unknown cause
cards.teaser: Federal regulators have not identified the source of infant botulism cases or determined how to prevent future infections.
cards.body:
The Food and Drug Administration continues to investigate an outbreak of infant botulism without having identified its cause or established prevention measures. The agency's investigation involves three companies, each of which has attributed responsibility to the others.

Botulism is a rare but serious illness caused by toxins that attack the nervous system. In infants, the condition can occur when babies ingest bacterial spores that produce toxins in the intestines. The FDA has not disclosed how many cases are linked to the outbreak.

cards.headline: Trump addresses farmers in Wisconsin on fertilizer and fuel costs
cards.teaser: President Trump visited Wisconsin to discuss rising agricultural costs with farmers, promising relief from high fertilizer and energy prices.
cards.body:
President Trump held a roundtable with farmers in Wisconsin on Friday to address surging fertilizer and fuel costs linked to U.S. military operations in Iran. He told farmers that fertilizer prices would drop to levels seen four months earlier once the conflict concludes.

The visit aimed to reassure agricultural producers facing economic pressure from increased input costs. During the event, Trump also discussed Washington topics including the Reflecting Pool and border policies, diverging from the primary agricultural focus of the meeting.

cards.headline: Putin declines meeting with Zelensky, calls Ukrainian letter rude
cards.teaser: The Russian president rejected his Ukrainian counterpart's call for face-to-face peace talks.
cards.body:
Russian President Vladimir Putin rejected a proposal from Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky for face-to-face negotiations to end the war. Speaking at an economic forum in St. Petersburg, Putin said there was "no point" in such a meeting and characterized Zelensky's open letter requesting talks as rude.

The refusal marks another setback in peace efforts as the conflict enters its third year. Putin's comments came amid Ukrainian drone attacks that have penetrated deep into Russian territory, reaching his hometown during the showcase economic gathering.

cards.headline: Ukrainian drone explodes at Romanian port after jamming diverts it off course
cards.teaser: Ukraine blamed Russian electronic warfare for pushing a maritime drone into NATO territory.
cards.body:
A Ukrainian maritime drone detonated at a Romanian Black Sea port with no injuries reported. Ukraine attributed the incident to Russian electronic warfare systems that disrupted the drone's navigation, causing it to divert into Romanian waters.

The explosion underscores the escalating risks from electronic jamming and GPS interference in the conflict. Romania, which shares a Black Sea border with Ukraine, has repeatedly encountered stray ordnance and debris from the fighting, raising ongoing concerns about the war's spillover effects into NATO territory.

cards.headline: Scientists say Russian satellites have been jamming GPS signals across Europe
cards.teaser: Researchers identified space-based interference with navigation systems dating back to 2019.
cards.body:
Russian satellites have been jamming GPS signals across Europe since 2019, according to scientists who traced the source of widespread navigation disruptions. The findings point to a sustained electronic warfare campaign conducted from orbit, affecting civilian and commercial GPS users across the continent.

Researchers said the jamming emanated from Russian satellites, marking a significant use of space assets for electronic interference. The disruptions have affected aviation, shipping, and other services that rely on satellite navigation. The revelation comes as electronic warfare has become an increasingly prominent feature of the conflict in Ukraine, with both sides deploying jamming systems to disrupt drones and communications.

cards.headline: France opens investigation into alleged Israeli mistreatment of Gaza flotilla activists
cards.teaser: Activists detained after attempting to reach Gaza said they faced abuse in Israeli custody.
cards.body:
French authorities have opened an investigation into allegations that Israeli forces mistreated pro-Palestinian activists detained after a flotilla attempted to reach Gaza. The activists claim they were abused while in Israeli custody following their interception.

Israeli authorities have denied the mistreatment allegations. The investigation underscores international attention on Israel's blockade of Gaza and its response to activist efforts to deliver aid to the territory.

cards.headline: Iran's soccer team receives US visas days before World Cup begins
cards.teaser: Players secured entry permits after months of uncertainty, though many staff were denied.
cards.body:
Iran's soccer players received visas to enter the United States just days before the World Cup begins, resolving months of uncertainty about the team's participation in the tournament. The last-minute approvals allow Iran's squad to compete in the event.

However, many staff members accompanying the team were denied entry permits, creating logistical challenges for the Iranian delegation. The visa situation reflects the strained diplomatic relationship between Washington and Tehran, which has complicated travel and interactions even for sporting events.

cards.headline: Jury hears testimony in Texas track meet stabbing trial
cards.teaser: Teen witnesses testified about a confrontation at a Frisco track meet that prosecutors say ended in murder.
cards.body:
The murder trial of 19-year-old Karmelo Anthony continues as he faces charges in the fatal stabbing of Austin Metcalf, a 17-year-old student, at a Frisco Independent School District track meet on April 2, 2025. Testimony from teenage witnesses has described the confrontation that led to the death, with prosecutors arguing the killing was murder while the defense maintains Anthony acted in self-defense.

The case has drawn nationwide attention amid discussions about racial tensions, as Anthony is Black and Metcalf was white. Jurors have viewed video footage from the incident at Kuykendall Stadium, with the trial now in its fourth day of witness testimony focusing on events surrounding the fatal confrontation.

cards.headline: FAA says Trump arch near Arlington will require aviation warning lights
cards.teaser: Federal aviation regulators determined the planned memorial arch near Arlington National Cemetery must have red lights for aircraft safety.
cards.body:
The Federal Aviation Administration has ruled that a planned arch honoring former President Trump near Arlington National Cemetery will need red warning lights due to its height. The decision addresses aviation safety concerns, though critics have raised separate objections about the structure affecting sightlines in the area. A planning chief argued the arch is not subject to Washington's building height limits.

Trump administration appointees voted to address what officials called gaps in the arch plan during what sources described as a heated meeting. The project has drawn opposition from those who say adding the arch to the capital's landscape would obstruct views. The structure cleared one regulatory hurdle despite ongoing concerns about its visual impact on the surrounding area.

cards.headline: Maine Senate candidate Graham Platner faces new allegations days before primary
cards.teaser: Several women who dated the Senate candidate described behavior they found unsettling, according to new reporting.
cards.body:
Graham Platner, a Maine Democratic Senate primary candidate, is denying accusations from multiple women who say he was physically rough during their relationships. The New York Times published accounts from several former girlfriends describing what they characterized as unsettling behavior.

Previous controversies involving Platner have included sexually explicit texts his wife flagged to his campaign. Despite the mounting allegations, Platner says he remains in the race, characterizing the reports as a sign his campaign is gaining momentum.

cards.headline: Israeli gunfire kills Palestinian baby in West Bank, health ministry says
cards.teaser: The Israeli military said the incident is under review and expressed sorrow for any harm caused.
cards.body:
A Palestinian baby was killed by Israeli gunfire in the West Bank on Friday, according to the Palestinian health ministry. The Israeli military acknowledged the shooting and said it is under review.

The military expressed what it described as deep sorrow for any harm caused. The incident contributes to ongoing violence in the West Bank between Israeli forces and Palestinians.

cards.headline: Mouse plagues devastate Australian farms, costing hundreds of thousands
cards.teaser: Rodent infestations are ravaging crops and invading homes across parts of Australia.
cards.body:
Australian farmers are suffering significant financial losses as mouse plagues ravage crops and invade homes across agricultural regions. Individual farmers report losses reaching hundreds of thousands of dollars as the rodents destroy harvests and stored grain. The infestations have also affected residential areas, with mice entering houses in large numbers.

The plagues represent a recurring problem in Australian agriculture, though the severity and frequency of outbreaks vary. Farmers face difficult decisions about pest control costs versus crop losses. The current wave of infestations has renewed questions about effective long-term management strategies for controlling mouse populations in agricultural areas.

cards.headline: Bulgarian singer Dara wins Eurovision after twice considering withdrawal
cards.teaser: The performer said her victory in Vienna nearly did not happen after she contemplated quitting twice.
cards.body:
Dara, representing Bulgaria with the song Bangaranga, won the Eurovision Song Contest in Vienna after coming close to withdrawing from the competition twice. The singer said the historic victory for Bulgaria nearly did not occur because she had seriously considered quitting before the final.

Dara did not specify what prompted her thoughts of withdrawal. Bulgaria had never won the Eurovision Song Contest before this year. The victory represents a significant achievement for the country in the annual competition, which draws performers and viewers from across Europe and beyond.

cards.headline: Google to Pay SpaceX Nearly $1 Billion Monthly in Cloud Computing Agreement
cards.teaser: Google agreed to pay SpaceX $920 million per month for artificial intelligence computing capacity at data centers.
cards.body:
Google reached a deal to pay SpaceX approximately $920 million each month for access to computing capacity at data centers operated by xAI, Elon Musk's artificial intelligence company. The agreement represents one of the largest cloud computing contracts disclosed publicly and comes as SpaceX prepares for a potential initial public offering.

The deal follows a similar arrangement between SpaceX and Anthropic, another artificial intelligence company. Google's substantial monthly payment underscores the intense demand for computing infrastructure to support AI development and the significant capital required to secure processing power at scale.

cards.headline: Trump Administration Considers Taking Equity Stakes in AI Companies
cards.teaser: President Donald Trump said the U.S. government may take ownership positions in artificial intelligence firms.
cards.body:
President Trump has indicated the U.S. government is exploring ownership stakes in artificial intelligence companies, including OpenAI and other AI startups. According to Trump, the administration views this as treating AI as a public resource and has scheduled meetings to discuss potential partnerships.

The proposal would represent a significant shift from how the government typically engages with technology companies. However, specifics about how the equity arrangements would work or what the government would provide in return have not been detailed.

cards.headline: States Prepare Lawsuit to Block Paramount Acquisition of Warner Bros.
cards.teaser: Ten state attorneys general are preparing antitrust litigation to challenge the proposed merger between Paramount and Warner Bros.
cards.body:
A coalition of U.S. states is preparing a lawsuit to block Paramount's proposed acquisition of Warner Bros. on antitrust grounds. At least ten states are involved in the effort to challenge the merger, which would combine two major entertainment studios. A Paramount lawyer responded to opponents by claiming some critics of the deal hold antisemitic views.

Paramount is seeking to have a separate lawsuit challenging the Warner Bros. acquisition dismissed, calling it a clumsy attempt to politicize antitrust litigation. Senator Elizabeth Warren has called for a foreign ownership review of the combined Paramount-Warner Bros. Discovery entity, adding another layer of scrutiny to the proposed transaction.

cards.headline: S&P 500 Index Rules Block Fast Entry for SpaceX and Other Large IPOs
cards.teaser: SpaceX faces a longer wait to join the S&P 500 index under new rules that prevent mega IPOs from immediate inclusion.
cards.body:
S&P Dow Jones Indices announced rules changes that will delay entry into the S&P 500 for large companies going public, directly affecting SpaceX's potential index inclusion timing. The new guidelines also block fast-track entry for other major private companies including OpenAI and Anthropic if they pursue initial public offerings.

The rule changes come as SpaceX prepares for what would be one of the largest IPOs in history. Critics note that SpaceX has reported significant financial losses, raising questions about forcing index fund investors to purchase shares in unprofitable companies regardless of the timing of index inclusion.

cards.headline: Elon Musk Tops List of Highest Paid Chief Executives
cards.teaser: Executive compensation is accelerating while rank-and-file worker pay lags, widening the corporate pay gap.
cards.body:
Elon Musk dominates the list of highest paid chief executives in corporate America, according to newly released compensation data. The figures show executive pay continuing to accelerate at the top of major corporations.

The compensation gap between executives and rank-and-file workers is widening as CEO pay packages grow at a faster pace than wages for typical employees. The disparity reflects ongoing trends in corporate compensation structures that concentrate financial rewards at the highest levels of management.

hero.headline: USB speaker exploited to hack PCs over Bluetooth without user interaction
hero.body:
Security researchers have discovered a critical vulnerability in Creative's Sound Blaster Katana V2X speaker that allows attackers to compromise connected computers through Bluetooth without requiring any user action. The exploit, named Pwnd Blaster, demonstrates how USB-connected speakers can serve as an attack vector for PC infections.

The attack leverages the speaker's dual connectivity, exploiting both its Bluetooth interface and USB connection to the host computer. When the speaker is connected to a PC via USB, an attacker can use Bluetooth to transmit malicious commands that compromise the machine. Notably, the victim does not need to interact with the device in any way, click links, or download files for the attack to succeed.

Creative has declined to treat this as a vulnerability. The company has made no announcement regarding plans to patch the issue or offer product recalls. The Sound Blaster Katana V2X is a widely used PC speaker priced at approximately $300.

Security professionals have raised significant concerns about the implications of this discovery. The ability to compromise a computer through a peripheral device without any user interaction represents a substantial security risk, particularly in corporate environments where multiple connected devices are attached to individual workstations. The vulnerability highlights how seemingly innocuous hardware can become a dangerous attack vector for malicious actors.

The revelation has prompted reassessment of connected peripherals among some users. Security researchers recommend that concerned users unplug microphones and speakers when they are not actively using them. For devices that support both USB and wireless connectivity, disabling Bluetooth functionality is another protective measure worth considering.

This discovery adds to mounting concerns about the security of Internet of Things devices and computer peripherals that combine multiple connectivity methods. As technology increasingly integrates wireless and wired connections, researchers warn that similar vulnerabilities may exist in other household and office devices.

The Pwnd Blaster exploit underscores a fundamental challenge in modern computing: the expanding attack surface created by interconnected devices. While individual peripherals may seem low-risk compared to other components, their privileged access to computer systems can make them attractive targets for sophisticated attackers.

Industry observers suggest that manufacturers need to prioritize security in device design rather than treating vulnerabilities as acceptable trade-offs. The situation with Creative's Sound Blaster Katana V2X demonstrates how a manufacturer's reluctance to acknowledge and address security flaws can leave users exposed to unnecessary risks.

For users who own this speaker model, the absence of an official patch means security depends on defensive measures like disconnecting the device or limiting its Bluetooth range until Creative chooses to address the issue.

cards.headline: Former IBM cyber executive alleges company covered up data breaches from mid-2010s
cards.teaser: A lawsuit filed by a former cybersecurity executive claims IBM and two subsidiaries failed to disclose breaches and actively concealed them.
cards.body:
A former cybersecurity executive has filed a lawsuit alleging that IBM and two subsidiary companies suffered data breaches in the mid-2010s without disclosing the incidents to affected parties or regulators.

According to the whistleblower's legal action, IBM actively concealed these security breaches rather than following required reporting procedures. The lawsuit documents multiple incidents during this period that allegedly compromised company and customer data.

cards.headline: Microsoft board member Reid Hoffman departs to focus on AI drug discovery startup
cards.teaser: LinkedIn co-founder Reid Hoffman is leaving Microsoft's board after a decade to concentrate on his artificial intelligence company Manus.
cards.body:
Reid Hoffman is stepping down from Microsoft's board of directors after a decade of service to focus on Manus, his AI drug discovery startup. His time on the Microsoft board proved financially lucrative for the technology investor.

By leaving the board, Hoffman can shift into "founder mode" and dedicate himself fully to Manus, which uses artificial intelligence to accelerate pharmaceutical research and development.

cards.headline: Astronomers detect wind from Milky Way's supermassive black hole after 50-year search
cards.teaser: Scientists have confirmed that the black hole at the center of our galaxy produces wind, solving a mystery that researchers have pursued for half a century.
cards.body:
Astronomers have detected wind emanating from Sagittarius A, the supermassive black hole at the center of the Milky Way galaxy. The discovery confirms a theoretical prediction that scientists have been trying to verify for 50 years.

The findings show that even relatively quiet black holes like Sagittarius A generate winds. Previous observations had detected winds from more active black holes in other galaxies, but the phenomenon at the Milky Way's center had remained elusive until now. The discovery provides new insights into how black holes interact with their surrounding environments.

cards.headline: Astronauts return to International Space Station after air leak repair attempt
cards.teaser: Five astronauts sheltered in place while Russian crew members attempted to fix an air leak in a tunnel area of the station.
cards.body:
Astronauts aboard the International Space Station have resumed normal duties after being placed on evacuation alert due to an air leak. NASA ordered four astronauts from the Crew-12 mission to enter their docked Crew Dragon spacecraft and don spacesuits as a precautionary measure while Russian specialists investigated the problem.

The air leaks were discovered in the Zveda module's transfer chamber during a pressurization procedure. After Russian teams assessed the situation, NASA cleared the crew to return to regular operations on Friday morning.

cards.headline: Capcom announces remake of Resident Evil Code Veronica for multiple platforms
cards.teaser: The survival horror game will be released as Resident Evil Veronica for Nintendo Switch 2, PlayStation 5, Xbox Series, and PC.
cards.body:
Capcom has announced a remake of Resident Evil Code Veronica, renaming it simply Resident Evil Veronica. The game will launch on Nintendo Switch 2, PlayStation 5, Xbox Series consoles, and PC next year.

The original Code Veronica was released in 2000 and followed the story of Claire Redfield. The remake continues Capcom's recent strategy of updating classic Resident Evil titles with modern graphics and gameplay mechanics for current gaming platforms.

hero.headline: Giants hit seven home runs in 18-3 rout of Cubs at Wrigley Field
hero.body:
The San Francisco Giants scored 18 runs and hit seven home runs in a blowout victory over the Chicago Cubs at Wrigley Field. The game marked Tony Vitello's debut at the historic ballpark and was delayed by rain before the Giants launched their offensive assault.

Matt Chapman led the Giants' attack with two home runs and a career-high eight runs batted in. The third baseman's performance powered San Francisco's dominant showing in what became one of the most lopsided games at Wrigley Field this season. The Giants' seven home runs in a single game represented a collective team effort that overwhelmed Cubs pitching from the early innings.

The Cubs managed only three runs in response to the Giants' offensive explosion. The 15-run margin of defeat marked a low point in Chicago's season as their pitching staff struggled to contain San Francisco's power hitters throughout the afternoon. The game took place during a rain delay before the Giants took control.

The victory improved the Giants' position as they continue their season, while the Cubs face questions about their pitching depth following the lopsided loss. Chapman's eight RBIs tied a personal best and highlighted his breakout performance in the series opener. The game's final score of 18-3 represented one of the largest margins in recent Cubs history at their home ballpark.

Both teams will look to regroup as the series continues. The Giants will aim to build on their offensive momentum, while the Cubs will need to stabilize their pitching to avoid another high-scoring defeat. The rain-delayed start gave way to a game that showcased the Giants' power-hitting capabilities and exposed vulnerabilities in the Cubs' pitching rotation.

cards.headline: Yankees place Aaron Judge on injured list with rib stress fracture
cards.teaser: The Yankees' star outfielder will be reevaluated in four to six weeks after fracturing his right rib on a diving play in late April.
cards.body:
Aaron Judge was diagnosed with a stress fracture in his right rib and placed on the injured list by the New York Yankees. The slugger will be reevaluated in four to six weeks, creating a significant gap in the Yankees' lineup during his absence.

Judge said the injury initially occurred on a diving play in late April but worsened over time. The Yankees face questions about how to replace his production in the lineup, with the injury affecting both their immediate playoff positioning and season outlook across the American League.

cards.headline: Bears board approves move to Hammond, Indiana for new stadium
cards.teaser: The Chicago Bears' board of directors voted to advance plans for a new stadium in Hammond, pushing the franchise across state lines.
cards.body:
The Chicago Bears board of directors has voted to advance plans for a new stadium in Hammond, Indiana, a move that shifts the franchise's focus away from Illinois after prolonged stadium negotiations. Hammond is located in the northwestern part of the state near the Illinois border.

The decision represents a major development following years of discussions about the team's future home. The vote comes after Arlington Heights, an Illinois suburb, had been considered as a potential stadium location.

cards.headline: Knicks and Spurs face off in NBA Finals Game 2
cards.teaser: The New York Knicks look to continue their streak as they meet the San Antonio Spurs in the second game of the NBA Finals.
cards.body:
The New York Knicks secured Game 1 of the NBA Finals at home, moving one step closer to their first championship in 53 years. San Antonio's Victor Wembanyama, the 7-foot-4-inch star, will be crucial to the Spurs' hopes of evening the series in Game 2, tipping off at 8:30 p.m. ET from the Frost Bank Center.

Jalen Brunson was instrumental in the Knicks' Game 1 victory. The Spurs must find adjustments as they look to bounce back in what amounts to a must-win situation if they hope to compete for the title against New York's momentum.

cards.headline: England suffer heaviest defeat in 17 years against Spain
cards.teaser: England lost heavily to Spain in a match that exposed defensive flaws, marking their worst loss since 2009.
cards.body:
England suffered their heaviest defeat in 17 years against Spain, despite only needing to avoid defeat in the match. The Spanish side overwhelmed England throughout the contest, exposing significant defensive vulnerabilities.

However, experts suggest there is no cause for alarm regarding England's form ahead of upcoming competitions. The loss, while painful for the squad, should not trigger panic about the team's future prospects.

cards.headline: Real Madrid prepare bid for Bayern Munich's Michael Olise
cards.teaser: The Spanish club is lining up a 130 million pound move for the Bayern winger as the summer transfer window heats up.
cards.body:
Real Madrid will launch a €150m (£130m) bid for Bayern Munich's Michael Olise if club president Florentino Pérez wins re-election this weekend. Olise is expected to be the club's top target in the summer transfer window.

In other transfer news, Arne Slot rejected an approach from Fulham following his departure from Liverpool. Newcastle United are close to completing their first summer signing as clubs across Europe advance their recruitment plans.

cards.headline: Iran players receive US visas for World Cup, staff members denied
cards.teaser: Iranian soccer players were granted entry to the United States for the 2026 World Cup, but many staff members had their visa applications rejected.
cards.body:
I can see the original card text references Iran's soccer team receiving US visas for the 2026 World Cup with staff denials, and mentions Tehrangeles and political tensions.

However, the additional source material provided consists of articles about England's transfer distractions and Chris Richards's injury—neither of which relate to Iran's visa situation or World Cup attendance.

Since the source material doesn't contain confirmed facts about the Iran visa story in the original card, I'm returning the original card text unchanged:

---

Iran's soccer team received approval to enter the United States for the 2026 World Cup, but many staff members were denied visas. The visa rejections and ongoing conflict have kept fans away from the tournament.

The World Cup previously triggered celebrations in Iran's streets, but the atmosphere feels different now. The Iranian diaspora community in Los Angeles, known as Tehrangeles, has a World Cup team to root against as political tensions continue to shape the tournament experience.

hero.headline: British Actor Anthony Head Dies at 72
hero.body:
Anthony Head, the acclaimed British actor best known for playing Rupert Giles in Buffy the Vampire Slayer, has died at age 72. He passed away peacefully from complications related to pneumonia, surrounded by his family, according to a statement from his daughters Emily and Daisy Head.

"It has been, and forever will be, an honour and a privilege to be his daughters, and to have witnessed first-hand the impact both he and his work have had on so many," they said.

Head's career spanned multiple decades and crossed both British and American entertainment industries. He achieved international recognition playing the mentor figure Giles, the school librarian and "watcher" to Sarah Michelle Gellar's character, throughout Buffy the Vampire Slayer's seven-season run from 1997 to 2003. The role made him a beloved figure among fans and helped define the mentor archetype in modern television fantasy.

Before becoming known to global audiences, Head had an extensive career in British entertainment. He began his professional work on the London stage, including a lead role in the 1988 West End production of the Abba musical Chess. He also starred as Dr Frank-N-Furter in the 1990 West End production of The Rocky Horror Show. Beyond theater, Head became widely recognized in the UK and US for appearing in Nescafé Gold Blend television advertisements throughout the 1980s.

His television work extended across multiple genres and productions. He took a recurring role in the BBC sketch comedy series Little Britain, playing a British prime minister constantly fawned over by a flirtatious assistant. He appeared in the BBC fantasy series Merlin and took on film roles in The Iron Lady and The Inbetweeners Movie. More recently, he joined the cast of Ted Lasso, the Apple TV+ comedy series, where he played former football club owner Rupert Mannion and developed on-screen chemistry with co-creator Jason Sudeikis.

Head was born in Camden, London, to artistic parents. His father founded Verity Films, a documentary company, while his mother was an actor who appeared in the 1960s BBC crime drama Maigret. His brother also pursued acting, earning a lead role in the 1971 film Sunday Bloody Sunday.

In an earlier interview with the Guardian, Head reflected on his childhood immersion in performance. "My Christmas present was always a new dressing-up outfit that my mother would make herself," he recalled. "At playgroup the woman who ran it took my parents aside one day and said, we love it when Anthony comes in dressing-up clothes, but it would be really nice to meet Anthony himself one day."

Head's daughters paid tribute to their father's legacy, noting that his grief is substantial but that his contributions will continue through the shows he appeared in and the audiences who love them. "How lucky we are to know we are able to watch him doing what he loved, even when he is no longer with us," they said.

cards.headline: Actor James Handy Killed in Stabbing, Girlfriend's Son Charged with Murder
cards.teaser: Character actor James Handy was stabbed to death in front of a Tarzana residence, and his girlfriend's son has been charged with murder.
cards.body:
James Handy, an 81-year-old veteran character actor known for roles in Top Gun: Maverick and Jumanji, died following a stabbing at his home in Tarzana, Los Angeles. He was found unconscious in his front yard on Wednesday morning with multiple stab wounds to the chest.

The son of Handy's girlfriend has been arrested and charged with murder in connection with the incident.

cards.headline: Final Fantasy VII Remake Trilogy to Conclude with Revelation in 2027
cards.teaser: Square Enix announced Final Fantasy VII: Revelation as the third and final game in its remake trilogy, set for spring 2027 release.
cards.body:
Square Enix has announced Final Fantasy VII: Revelation as the final installment in its remake trilogy, launching in spring 2027 across PC, PS5, Xbox Series X|S, and Nintendo Switch 2. The announcement included gameplay footage shown at Summer Game Fest Live.

The trilogy reimagines the 1997 classic RPG with expanded storytelling and modernized graphics and mechanics. Revelation will bring the narrative arc to a close following the first two games in the series.

cards.headline: Animated Among Us Series Drops on Paramount+ Without Prior Notice
cards.teaser: All 10 episodes of the animated Among Us television series became available on Paramount+ in a surprise release.
cards.body:
Paramount+ released the entire first season of the animated Among Us television series without advance warning. All 10 episodes are now available to stream on the platform. Voice actors Yvette Nicole Brown and Liv Hewson announced the surprise drop at Summer Game Fest in Los Angeles.

The series is based on the popular multiplayer video game Among Us, which became a cultural phenomenon during its rise to prominence. The unexpected release strategy marks a departure from traditional marketing rollouts for new animated series. No prior promotional campaign had indicated the show would debut at this time.

cards.headline: Sean Penn Skipped Oscars Despite Winning Third Academy Award
cards.teaser: Sean Penn won Best Supporting Actor at the recent Academy Awards but did not attend the ceremony due to his aversion to large public gatherings.
cards.body:
Sean Penn was absent from the 98th Academy Awards despite winning Best Supporting Actor, his third Oscar. In a recent interview with CNN anchor Kaitlin Collins, Penn explained he refuses to attend public gatherings with more than eight people. He also stated he will not take selfies with anyone under any circumstances.

Penn's Oscar win marks his third Academy Award. His refusal to attend the ceremony aligns with his stated preferences about public appearances. The actor has maintained these personal boundaries regardless of the significance of the event or the individuals involved, including Holocaust survivors who might request photos.

cards.headline: Love Island USA Season 8 Sets Peacock Viewership Record
cards.teaser: The eighth season of Love Island USA has become the most-watched original television debut in Peacock's history.
cards.body:
Season 8 of Love Island USA became Peacock's most-watched original television debut ever. Following its June 2 premiere, the first three episodes accumulated 824 million minutes watched across the platform.

The strong performance reflects shifting viewing habits, with 23 percent of viewers watching on mobile devices rather than traditional screens. The reality dating show has emerged as a major driver of engagement for the NBCUniversal streaming service.

cards.headline: Paramount Games Studio Announces First Project Based on Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles
cards.teaser: Paramount Games Studio revealed Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles: The Last Ronin as its inaugural project at Summer Game Fest.
cards.body:
Paramount Games Studio, the combined in-house development studio of Paramount and Skydance, unveiled its first project at Summer Game Fest: Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles: The Last Ronin. Platinum Games is developing the title, which will be published by Paramount Games Studio.

The game is a AAA action-adventure title based on the Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles franchise. This announcement marks Paramount's entry into direct game development and publishing, leveraging Platinum Games' experience creating action games for major entertainment properties.

hero.headline: Defense Secretary Hegseth brings six children on France trip
hero.teaser: Secretary of Defense Hegseth traveled to France with six of his children on an official visit, raising concerns about security strain.
hero.body:
Defense Secretary Hegseth brought six of his children to France on an official trip, according to Pentagon officials. The Pentagon stated that Hegseth is covering his family's travel expenses personally.

Despite the personal payment arrangement, officials warned that bringing family members along could strain his security team during a period of increased threats. The trip occurred as the defense secretary conducted official business in France.

cards.headline: Federal prosecutor opens election fraud investigations in California
cards.teaser: A federal prosecutor has launched multiple investigations into alleged voter fraud following President Trump's accusations of cheating in the state's primary elections.
cards.body:
Bill Essayli, the first assistant U.S. attorney for the Central District of California, announced Friday that his office had opened multiple election fraud investigations following President Trump's accusations that Democrats cheated in the state's primary elections.

The Justice Department also sent a federal prosecutor to observe ballot processing in Los Angeles. State officials have rejected Trump's allegations of rigging. California's vote counting has extended beyond election day, with experts warning the process could take weeks or even a month to complete for races including governor, LA mayor, and congressional seats.

cards.headline: Trump addresses farmers in Wisconsin on fertilizer and fuel costs
cards.teaser: President Trump visited Wisconsin to discuss rising agricultural costs with farmers, promising relief from high fertilizer and energy prices.
cards.body:
President Trump held a roundtable with farmers in Wisconsin on Friday to address surging fertilizer and fuel costs linked to U.S. military operations in Iran. He told farmers that fertilizer prices would drop to levels seen four months earlier once the conflict concludes.

The visit aimed to reassure agricultural producers facing economic pressure from increased input costs. During the event, Trump also discussed Washington topics including the Reflecting Pool and border policies, diverging from the primary agricultural focus of the meeting.

cards.headline: Chief of staff for Texas congressman charged with firearm violations
cards.teaser: Luis Vega, chief of staff to Rep. Pete Sessions, faces two counts after allegedly attempting to bring a firearm into the U.S. Capitol complex.
cards.body:
Luis Vega, chief of staff for Rep. Pete Sessions of Texas, was charged Wednesday with two firearm-related counts. The charges stem from an alleged incident in which Vega attempted to bring a firearm into the U.S. Capitol complex days before Christmas last year.

The case involves violations of Capitol security protocols, which prohibit unauthorized firearms in congressional buildings. Sessions, a Republican congressman, has not publicly commented on the charges against his top staffer.

cards.headline: US military shoots down Iranian drones, strikes coastal radar sites
cards.teaser: The U.S.
cards.body:
The U.S. military shot down four Iranian one-way attack drones on Friday that were heading toward the Strait of Hormuz and posed an imminent threat to maritime traffic, according to U.S. Central Command. After the interception, U.S. forces struck Iranian coastal surveillance radar sites in Goruk, a city in Hormozgan province, and on Qeshm Island.

The action comes amid ongoing tensions between the United States and Iran, which have escalated following U.S. military operations in the region. The Strait of Hormuz is a critical waterway through which about one-fifth of the world's oil passes, making it a strategic flashpoint. Iranian drone activity in the area has previously threatened commercial shipping lanes.

Centcom described the drones as one-way attack drones, a type of unmanned aircraft designed to strike targets by crashing into them. The military assessed that the drones presented an imminent threat to vessels transiting the strait, prompting the decision to engage. The subsequent strikes on radar installations aimed to degrade Iran's ability to monitor and target shipping in the area.

The incident reflects the broader military confrontation between Washington and Tehran. President Trump has referenced the conflict as the U.S. war in Iran during recent public appearances, including a Friday roundtable with farmers in Wisconsin where he discussed rising fertilizer and fuel costs tied to the military operations. The administration has not detailed the full scope of U.S. military engagement in the region.

Neither the Pentagon nor Iranian officials immediately provided casualty figures from the radar site strikes. The Iranian government has not yet issued a public response to the U.S. military action. The engagement marks the latest in a series of confrontations in and around the Strait of Hormuz, where U.S. and Iranian forces have clashed repeatedly over freedom of navigation and regional security.

cards.headline: House Democrat calls on Maine Senate candidate to exit race
cards.teaser: Rep. Madeleine Dean said Democratic Senate candidate Graham Platner has disqualified himself following allegations about his past behavior toward women.
cards.body:
Rep. Madeleine Dean of Pennsylvania said Friday that Democrat Graham Platner has "disqualified himself" from the Maine Senate race. Her remarks came as allegations about Platner's past behavior toward women continued to surface.

Platner is seeking the Democratic nomination for Maine's Senate seat. Dean expressed concern about the escalating nature of the accusations, noting that new allegations were appearing regularly. The growing scrutiny has drawn attention from members of his own party.

cards.headline: Deb Haaland wins New Mexico Democratic primary for governor
cards.teaser: Former Biden administration official Deb Haaland secured the Democratic nomination in New Mexico's gubernatorial primary.
cards.body:
Deb Haaland, a former Biden administration official, won New Mexico's Democratic primary for governor on Friday. She will be the Democratic nominee in the general election this November.

If elected, Haaland would make history as the first female Native American governor in the United States. She will face the Republican nominee in the race to lead New Mexico.
